name: flate2
reason: DEFLATE/gzip for the M4 zip and gzip sentences. Compared libz-sys (C zlib; tier B, needs a system zlib on Linux) and inflate-only crates (several unmaintained forks). flate2 wins on maturity, pure-Rust miniz_oxide backend, maintenance and a permissive dual license (MIT/Apache-2.0; the MIT option is recorded).

name: jiff
reason: Time zones, dates and moments (M4-7, Appendix K 7.7). Compared chrono + chrono-tz (two crates; chrono-tz ships a huge generated table and chrono needs a separate zone source on every OS) and hand-writing zone handling (rejected: real IANA rules). jiff wins: the zone database ships INSIDE the crate (jiff-tzdb, IANA 2026e) on every OS with default-features = false, the API is ergonomic, maintenance is active, and the license is a permissive Unlicense/MIT dual (the Unlicense option is recorded).

name: object
reason: ELF/COFF object writing for the native backend (M3). Compared goblin (slower releases, more scope) and writing COFF/ELF by hand (done for M3-M4 zip, not for object files with relocations). object wins: the Rust toolchain itself uses it, Apache-2.0/MIT dual.

name: rustls
reason: TLS for the M4 network sentences (Appendix K 7.8: S61 the client checks certificates against the bundled root store; S64 Serve securely uses rustls BY NAME in the spec). rustls is the TLS stack the ecosystem standardizes on; alternatives: native-tls/schannel (OS store, not the bundled one) and openssl-sys (C OpenSSL, not permissive). rustls is pure Rust over a vetted crypto provider, Apache-2.0/ISC/MIT tri-license (Apache-2.0 recorded).

name: rustls-pemfile
reason: PEM reading for Serve securely (M4-S64: the certificate file and key file are PEM files). The standard companion of rustls; Apache-2.0/ISC/MIT (Apache-2.0 recorded).

name: serde

name: serde_json
reason: JSON read/save (M4-G49). Compared json (no serde integration) and simd-json (runtime flags). serde_json wins on maturity and ecosystem fit.

name: sha2
reason: SHA-256 for the hash of X sentence (M4-7, Appendix K 7.7; previously declared in M3 for the native backend). Compared ring (bigger scope, build complexity) and hand-writing (rejected: the spec asks for real SHA-256). sha2 is the standard pure-Rust implementation, MIT/Apache-2.0 dual.

name: signal-hook
reason: Signal flag registration for the M4 system sentences (Appendix K 7.10: When signal ... arrives.; interrupt/stop/hangup flags polled at sentence boundaries). Compared the unsafe libc handler approach (rejected: signal-safety rules make it easy to get wrong) and ctrlc (a different crate, defaults to a process exit instead of a pollable flag). signal-hook wins: the flag module registers per-signal ATOMIC FLAGS (no unsafe in our code, no process exit, the interpreter polls at its own pause points), maintenance is active, and the license is a permissive MIT/Apache-2.0 dual. Its dependencies libc and signal-hook-registry are platform shims.

name: unicode-normalization
reason: The Book requires normalized texts (De-5). Unicode data cannot be reimplemented otherwise; this is the reference crate of the ecosystem. Note: its data files carry the Unicode-3.0 license alongside MIT/Apache-2.0 code (flagged verify until the owner ratifies Unicode-3.0 as an allowed tier-B-equivalent).
